construction: 68 parts in 10 root steps and two children. Steps 1–2: a strip of 1×8 and 1×4 plates. Steps 3–7: 1×4 bricks and 1×1 bricks stacked three high with the 60581 reinforced panel and a 1×2 brick in the middle. Steps 8–10: the 2429/2430 hinge plates at each end, plates on top and the 60583b clip brick with a string-end stud; the `string5` child is the rigging string.
interfaces: All studs up; the string angled. The hinge plates at the ends are the interface to the neighbouring fuselage walls; the plate strip's underside sits on the fuselage floor.
lesson: A biplane fuselage side as a one-stud-thick wall: dark-tan 1×4 and 1×1 bricks on a 1×8 plate strip, two 1×4 hinge-plate pairs so the wall folds to the fuselage taper, a reinforced 1×4×3 panel as the cockpit side, and a 1×1×3 clip brick that anchors a rigging string.
parent_context: `10226 - main.ldr` places it at (60, −16, 60) with matrix −1 0 0 / 0 1 0 / 0 0 −1, a 180° turn about Y, as the right-hand fuselage side beside the cockpit; `step35` is the mirrored left side.
reuse_notes: Rebuild the technique: a one-stud wall with hinge plates at the ends lets a plate-built fuselage taper in plan; use a reinforced panel where the wall needs to be thin but stiff.
